td._comment_chain: approachChain is the berth order a train steps through on the way IN, nearest-last. It gives (a) the set of berths whose strike-in is recorded, and (b) an ordering so the CLOSED backstop can tell whether a train is still upstream of its close anchor. Derived from TD step order (see the berth-chain derivation) and verified against SMART.

schedule._comment_tiploc_station: TIPLOC of the crossing's OWN station (Portslade, CRS PLD — verified against CORPUS; note it is PSLDAWH, not PORTSLD). Used only to read whether a CIF schedule CALLS here (arrival/departure present) or merely passes, so a passenger service beyond the ~2h LDB window is classified correctly instead of defaulting to non-stopping.
schedule._comment_tiploc_approach_call: SOUTHWICK (CORPUS-verified STHWICK) sits INSIDE eastbound approach berth 0006. Services calling there spend a median 160s in 0006 (range 124-203) against 49s (44-79) for those that don't — two disjoint populations, so the 0006 strike-in means completely different things depending on the calling pattern. VALIDATED against a full day of TD: this flag reproduces the observed split with 0 mismatches in 93 runs. (Fishersgate, also on this stretch, does NOT split it — 41/93 mismatches — so do not swap it back on the assumption that the nearest station is the relevant one.) Read from the CIF schedule for every service, then applied to LDB-sourced trains by UID/headcode.

timing._comment_openAfterSecs: Far-out barrier-up fallback, SECONDS, superseding openAfter (minutes, kept for other crossings / rollback). Split by what bestTime is ANCHORED TO, because one number cannot serve both sources. crossingAnchored = CIF trains: bestTime is estimatedCrossingMins, or _projectBerth(XING) once a berth exists, so the open is bestTime + openLagSecs (east 40 / west 20, rounded from the field-calibrated 18). stationAnchored = LDBSVWS trains: bestTime is Darwin's time at Portslade STATION, and eastbound the crossing is BEFORE the platform, so the open lands BEFORE bestTime — measured east median -21s / west +55s over the 3 Aug audit, n=100. Was a single +30s both directions with no provenance, which made every east closure ~50s too long and drove the C15m over-merging. Only governs trains with NO live berth; superseded per berth strike once the projected-open rung lands.

openLagSecs._comment: Anchored to TD clear-step time, NOT bestTime. Derived from 24 Jun 2026 observer session cross-checked against FOI (auto-raise on FM/AC track-circuit clear). passenger west n=6 (obs 15-23s), re-measured 29-30 Jul n=3 (12,15,29) and again 1 Aug n=5 (14,16,20,21,24) -> pooled n=8 by the uniform TD method, mean 18.9, median 18, sd 5.3, so 18 CONFIRMED TWICE, do not retune; freight east n=2; freight west n=0 DELIBERATE GUESS.
openLagSecs._comment_east_passenger: 45 -> 35 on 2026-07-31, 35 -> 40 on 2026-08-02. History: 45 was never measured (24 Jun saw 36-43s, n=4, and 45 was a safety margin); the 29-30 Jul session re-measured barrier-up minus the train's own 0002 clear step as 23,30,32,32,42,46 (n=6, mean 34) and 35 was adopted. The 1 Aug session gave 43,48,51 (n=3) — every value above 35 and above the 45 it had just replaced. Re-derived uniformly against the TD log across all three sessions: n=9, mean 38.6, median 42, sd 9.0, range 23-51. 40 is that pooled mean rounded to the sd. The two sessions are NOT contradictory, they sample different hours: peak (07-09, 17-19) n=6 mean 43.7, early afternoon n=3 mean 28.3. Two candidate mechanisms, both consistent and neither yet separated — peak formations are longer, and the auto-raise fires on rear-of-train track-circuit clear, so a 12-car takes measurably longer to clear than a 4-car after the same 0002 strike. If that is the cause the right fix is a length or formation term, not a single mean; 40 is the best single number until length is recorded. NOT split by stopping/through: hinted at, still not evidenced.

closeTrigger._comment: CLOSE start = per-class berth strike-in + offset. EASTBOUND USES PER-CLASS ANCHORS because approach berth 0006 CONTAINS SOUTHWICK: services calling there sit in 0006 for ~150s, those that don't for ~50s, so one anchor cannot serve both. Measured over 7,579 eastbound runs / 77 days of TD logs (2026-07-25). Offsets = median(berth->crossing) - LEAD, where LEAD is the observed barrier-down lead before the crossing. Cross-check: the same arithmetic reproduces class B's independently field-calibrated +100s as +106s. UPDATED 2026-08-02: the 140s LEAD was never a property of eastbound traffic — every one of the three 24 Jun taps it came from (127/152/257) was a SOUTHWICK-CALLER, because class A had zero barrier observations at the time. It was then applied to all five classes. The 1 Aug session separates the populations for the first time: stoppingLocal 127,152,149,131 -> mean 140 sd 11 n=4 (the 1 Aug pair corroborates 140 and isolates the 257 as an outlier), stopping 58,98,130 -> mean 95 sd 30 n=3. So 140 is CONFIRMED for stoppingLocal and does not transfer. fast/ecs are non-Southwick classes still carrying it — treat their offsets as UNFOUNDED, not provisional.
closeTrigger._comment_east_classes: stopping = calls Portslade, NOT Southwick (1H Victoria semi-fasts): 0008->xing med 189s sd 28, n=2228; anchored 0008+55 (40 -> 55 on 2026-08-02, Rich's call). FIRST barrier observations for this class: residuals against the old +40 were +130, +46, +5 — every one the same sign, the rule closing a mean 60s EARLY. Two readings of why, and 55 is inside both: if the 95s lead measured on these three is a class property, median-unbiased is 189-95 = +94; if the lead is really 140 for all east traffic, median-unbiased is the +49 this entry already quoted. 40 is outside that range at both ends. 55 leaves residuals +115, +31, -10 — still early on two of three, and the 10s late case is well inside safetyNetSecs(145) and the confidence band. CAVEAT: the class split rests mostly on the two 29 Jul trains (58, 98); within 1 Aug alone the classes gave 130 vs 131/149, indistinguishable. That is why 55 and not 94. Settle it with 3-4 more 1H east closes, ideally one session catching both classes back-to-back so the lead comparison is within-session. NOTE 0006 is UNUSABLE for this class — its strike lands a median 29s AFTER the barrier is already down, which was the pre-2026-07-25 bug. stoppingLocal = calls Portslade AND Southwick (1N/1S/2Y Brighton services): 0006->xing med 246s sd 58, n=4542; 0006+100 UNCHANGED, and re-confirmed 2026-08-02 — DO NOT retune it on the 1 Aug residuals (-48s on 1N07, +86s on 2Y53), which look bad and are not. Feed each train's ACTUAL transit into close = crossing - 140 and both land within 10s: 1N07 202-140 = 62 vs 52 observed, 2Y53 318-140 = 178 vs 186 observed. The whole residual is the median transit (246, sd 58) being wrong for that run, which no offset value can fix — only a sharper crossing estimate would. Median-unbiased is 246-140 = +106, so the shipped 100 is ~6s early, the intended bias. Provenance: 24 Jun n=5 cluster 80-113s, plus the n=4 lead above. fast = calls neither Portslade nor Southwick, passenger: 0008->xing med 158s sd 68, n=256 — WEAK, the analysis classifier was contaminated. ecs = 5xxx: 0008->xing med 226s sd 83, n=522 — WEAK. freight = 6xxx/7xxx: 0006->xing med 161s sd 55, n=31 over 5 headcodes; freight is ~100s SLOWER than fast passenger at every berth so it must NOT share their rule. Class A HAD zero barrier observations (for 1H services the barrier is often already down on arrival, so the observer rarely logs a separate CLOSE — that selection bias is what produced the original +100s error). It now has three: 1H15 29 Jul, 1H57 29 Jul, 1H13 1 Aug. Still want 3-4 more; they cross ~xx:15 and ~xx:45.
closeTrigger._comment_safetynet: safetyNetSecs.east 210 -> 145. 210 was sized against a claimed ~280s strike lead that measurement showed to be 149s, so the backstop fired BEFORE the anchor for 34/34 class-A trains — it was the primary close path, not a backstop. 145 puts it ~30s AFTER the class-A anchor (0008->bestTime min 212s observed, anchor at +185s relative) so the precise strike wins. Side effect, intended: safetyNet now < predictedLeadSecs (145 < 180), so the confirmed close is LATER than the predicted one and the frontend 'Soon' state stops being dormant. Cost on a genuinely missed strike (measured 0.093% of crossings) is CLOSED ~20-30s later. Also gated by position — see approachChain.

east._comment_confirmedMayFollowPredicted: Opt-in: allow the CLOSED gate to sit LATER than the predicted close. True only here, because safetyNetSecs(145) < predictedLeadSecs(180) is deliberate eastbound — it is what makes the frontend 'Soon' state live instead of dormant. Everywhere else the backstop is clamped to the prediction, so a pair of unrelated config values can't silently produce a window where the countdown has passed zero while the app still says CLEAR.

west._comment: BERTH-ANCHORED since 2026-08-01 (was `departure - 45s`). offsetSecs = transit[berth>XING] - 92s, where 92s is the observed close lead (crossing minus barrier-down) from n=11 westbound barrier observations (8 on 24 Jun, 3 on 31 Jul). The ANCHOR is well grounded, the OFFSET is not: over n=771 westbound crossings the berth strikes predict the crossing 2.5x better than Darwin's departure estimate (sd: 0005 19.6s, 0003 21.7s, liveDep 48.8s, schedDep 253s). 0003 chosen over 0005 despite the marginally better sd because it fires earlier and stays feasible. Deliberately NO dwell term — three measurements killed it: CIF booked dwell has only two values (30/60s) against realised 0-180s; refitting on booked gave sd 61s, WORSE than the old rule's 43s; and subtracting live dwell DOUBLED sd (13.5 -> 25.8s) because it is the difference of two minute-rounded times. Raw 0005>XING sd of 19.6s cannot contain minutes of dwell variance, so there is nothing to remove.
west._comment_lead: crossingLeadSecs is the ONE calibrated number here: the observed seconds between barrier-down and the train reaching the crossing, from n=11 westbound barrier observations. Each class's offset is DERIVED at runtime as transit[berth>XING] - crossingLeadSecs, so it follows the transit table when that is regenerated instead of drifting away from it. Only the anchor BERTH is per class, chosen so the derived offset stays positive: a rule cannot fire before the strike it is anchored to.
west._comment_prestrike: predictedDepartureLeadSecs is the PRE-STRIKE prediction, used only while TD cannot place the train at all — the westbound analogue of east predictedLeadSecs. 46s because for an LDB westbound bestTime IS the departure estimate, the crossing follows it by a measured 46s (sd 16s, n=8), and the close leads the crossing by 92s. A CIF westbound falls to crossingLeadSecs instead, because its bestTime is an interpolated CROSSING time, not a departure. Dropping this and letting closeBefore take over moved an unplaceable train's close 105s early and re-merged periods the clear-step merge key separates.

stopping._derived: 153-92 = +61s. anchor n=771 (crossing-0003 = 156s, sd 22s); lead n=11. 95.2% of westbound traffic

freight._derived: 121-92 = +29s. transit n=37; one barrier observation gives 0003+39s, within 10s. 0.5%

ecs._derived: 148-92 = +56s. transit n=266; barrier lead n=0 GUESS. 0003 would be -3s, infeasible. 3.5%

fast._derived: 94-92 = +2s. transit n=60; barrier lead n=0 GUESS, and FRAGILE — fires ~instantly on the strike, so pipeline latency eats the margin. 0003 would be -39s. 0.8%

west._comment_unknown: A train whose class cannot be resolved falls to `stopping` (see _classOf/_eastClass fallbacks), which is the right default: 95% of westbound traffic is stopping.
